meta.title: Predicted physics
meta.subtitle: A rigid body solver re-clocked onto the prediction tick, and the two things that correct it

views.label: The clock domain crossing
views.note: Physics is moved out of the fixed-step group and driven by the prediction tick instead.

views.label: What corrects a body
views.note: Only replicated fields are restored. Everything else keeps whatever the replay left.

views.label: The render pose
views.note: Between ticks the body does not move; smoothing fills the gap and is never read back.

nodes.label: PredictedSimulation
nodes.sublabel: one edge per tick, many per frame

cards.title: Why the solver moved groups
items: FixedStep is driven by a wall clock accumulator, once per frame
Prediction needs the same tick solved again after every correction
PredictedPhysicsConfigSystem relocates the group once, then removes itself
Ordering you wrote against FixedStep is now in a different group

cards.title: Two gates, both must open
items: The prediction loop runs only when predicted ghosts exist, by default
The physics group then applies PhysicGroupRunMode on top of that
This is why a raycast against static geometry returns nothing early on
AlwaysRun on both is the fix, and it costs an update every frame

cards.title: What rollback does not restore
items: Only fields carrying a GhostField are copied back
PhysicsMass, gravity factor and collider blobs are not replicated
Mutate one inside prediction and the change applies once per replayed tick
It looks correct until the first packet drops

cards.title: The cost, and the emergency valve
items: Cost is predicted bodies times replayed ticks, times a full solve
Batch repeated ticks before batching first-time ticks
Batching integrates a larger delta, so contacts resolve differently
Prefer shrinking the predicted set over batching it
